skills.name: Next.js Image Optimization
skills.description: Optimize images in Next.js applications using the built-in `next/image` component to reduce file size, improve load performance, and enable responsive sizing with automatic format conversion.
skills.skill_body: Use the `next/image` component to wrap image assets. Configure responsive sizing via width/height props or fill layout. Enable lazy loading (default) and automatic format selection (WebP, AVIF). Verify images are served with appropriate srcset and lazy-loading attributes. ## Objective reduce_image_payload_and_render_time ## Applicable Signals - Multiple image assets in application - Performance metrics show image payload as bottleneck - Need for responsive image delivery across device sizes ## Contraindications - Images already optimized externally or via third-party CDN with no Next.js integration required - Static images served directly from public directory without component wrapping ## Intervention Moves - Import Image component from next/image - Replace standard tags with component - Set src, alt, width, and height props or use fill layout - Configure priority, sizes, or quality props as needed - Verify responsive srcset and lazy loading in browser DevTools ## Workflow Steps - Import Image component from next/image - Replace standard tags with component - Set src, alt, width, and height props (or use fill layout) - Optionally configure priority, sizes, or quality props - Verify responsive srcset and lazy loading in browser DevTools ## Constraints - Images must be imported or have explicit dimensions (width/height) or fill layout - next/image component requires Next.js 10.0.0 or later ## Cautions - Lazy loading is enabled by default; use priority prop only for above-the-fold images to avoid performance regression - Ensure image dimensions are set correctly to prevent layout shift ## Output Contract - Images are served with automatic format selection, responsive srcset attributes, and lazy loading enabled by default. Caller receives optimized image delivery with reduced payload and improved render performance.

skills.name: Next.js Font Loading Optimization
skills.description: Optimize web fonts using the built-in `next/font` loaders to reduce font file size, improve text rendering performance, and eliminate layout shift during font load.
skills.skill_body:
Use the built-in `next/font` loaders to configure and optimize web fonts in your Next.js application. Configure font subsetting, preloading, and fallback strategies to ensure fonts load efficiently without causing cumulative layout shift (CLS).

## Objective

reduce_font_payload_and_improve_text_rendering
## Applicable Signals

- Custom font files referenced in layout or page components
- Multiple font weights or variants required
- Performance audit flags font-related CLS or LCP issues

## Contraindications

- System fonts only (no custom fonts needed)
- Fonts already optimized via external CDN with proper caching
- Font files served from third-party provider with built-in optimization

## Workflow Steps

- {'step': 2, 'action': 'Configure next/font loader', 'detail': 'Import and configure font loader with appropriate subsetting and weight options'}
- {'step': 3, 'action': 'Apply font to layout or page component', 'detail': 'Assign loaded font to CSS class or style variable for use in components'}
- {'step': 4, 'action': 'Define fallback font stack', 'detail': 'Ensure fallback fonts match loaded font metrics to minimize layout shift'}
- {'step': 5, 'action': 'Verify preloading and subset behavior', 'detail': 'Test font loading in browser DevTools; confirm no CLS during font load'}

## Constraints

- Font loader configuration must be applied at layout or page level
- Subsetting strategy should match actual character usage in application
- Fallback font stack must be defined to prevent layout shift

## Cautions

- Ensure font preloading does not conflict with other resource priorities
- Test font loading behavior across network conditions (slow 3G, 4G)
- Verify no duplicate font requests after optimization

## Output Contract

- Fonts are preloaded and subset automatically
- No cumulative layout shift (CLS) occurs during font load
- Font file size is reduced through subsetting
- Text renders with optimized font without blocking page interaction

skills.name: Third-Party Script Performance Optimization
skills.description: Optimize third-party scripts (analytics, ads, tracking) using the built-in Script component to control loading strategy and prevent main-thread blocking.
skills.skill_body:
Use the built-in Script component to wrap third-party scripts and apply appropriate loading strategies. Choose from beforeInteractive (critical, blocks render), afterInteractive (default, non-blocking), or lazyOnload (deferred until interaction). This prevents scripts from blocking the main thread and improves overall page performance.

## Objective

reduce_third_party_script_impact_on_performance
## Applicable Signals

- presence of Google Analytics, ad networks, or tracking pixels
- performance metrics show script-related rendering delays
- build optimization phase or performance improvement initiative

## Contraindications

- Scripts are critical for initial page render or above-the-fold content
- Scripts are already optimized via external loader or CDN strategy
- Script execution order is tightly coupled and cannot be deferred

## Intervention Moves

- wrap external script with built-in Script component
- assign appropriate loading strategy based on script criticality
- test page rendering and script functionality
- monitor performance metrics and adjust strategies

## Workflow Steps

- Identify all third-party scripts in the application
- Classify each script by criticality: critical (beforeInteractive), standard (afterInteractive), or deferred (lazyOnload)
- Wrap each script with the built-in Script component and assign the appropriate strategy
- Test page rendering and script functionality with each strategy
- Monitor performance metrics and script execution timing
- Adjust strategies based on performance data and functional requirements

## Constraints

- Script component must wrap the external script tag
- Loading strategy must match script criticality and use case
- Verify script functionality after applying deferred loading

## Cautions

- beforeInteractive strategy blocks page render; use only for truly critical scripts
- lazyOnload may delay analytics or tracking data collection; monitor data completeness
- Test script behavior across different loading strategies before production deployment

## Output Contract

- Scripts are loaded according to assigned strategy; main thread is unblocked for non-critical scripts; performance metrics (LCP, FID, CLS) show improvement or remain stable; all scripts execute correctly and collect data as expected.
